name: p01
prompt:
Hand-inked watercolor storybook animation in the ink line, paper grain and palette of the reference images. Three beats, one continuous film.

Beat 1 (0-3s), Turkey's seat: the fixed eye-level view inside the bread-roll-tin submarine exactly as in the cockpit reference: centered brass six-bolt porthole with a chip at two o'clock, empty ballast slot at lower left, chalk route chart under glass at lower center, brass lamp toggle at lower right, amber lamp overhead, dent in the right wall. Outside the glass is only murky blue-green silt and one huge dark shape. A feathered turkey wing reaches in from the lower right foreground and flips the brass lamp toggle.

Beat 2 (3-7s): an amber beam switches on below the porthole and the camera pushes slowly in to the glass. The silt clears to the scene of the porthole reference: a giant size-eleven dark rubber boot standing on the riverbed, blocking the beam, backlit into a silhouette. It shifts its weight and a puff of silt rolls off the sole. A faint reflection of the turkey's face on the glass tilts, puzzled.

Beat 3 (7-10s), hard cut across the glass to the outside view of the reference: the riveted metal tin on the riverbed, the turkey small behind the amber porthole, and in the foreground a speckled brook trout beside the towering boot, turning to stare in at the turkey; the amber beam lights the boot sole like a flashlight.

Bubbles rise throughout. No text, no labels, no captions.

Beat 3 (7-10s), hard cut across the glass to the outside view of the reference: the riveted metal tin on the riverbed, lit amber like a covered roasting dish and like a landed saucer, the turkey small behind the porthole turning a little valve with one wing tip. In the foreground the trout cook dribbles the silver baster along the tin's lid, then taps a rivet with it like a plumber, head cocked.

In the foreground, low in frame as the pupils are in the fourth reference, two young trout with satchels by the chalkboard: one swims up and holds out a worm to the glass, the other ducks behind the board frame, pointing a fin from the sketch to the turkey.
